case.name: Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology Co., Ltd.
case.constructed: An Alibaba.com buyer orders 2,000 IP cameras from a listing that names Hikvision as the manufacturer. The supplier is real; the proforma invoice is constructed: it asks for the 30% deposit by direct bank transfer outside Trade Assurance, to a Hong Kong account held by a trading company whose name is not the supplier's.

expect.why: The deposit would leave Trade Assurance and go to an account in another company's name, and the supplier sits on US export-control and non-SDN sanctions lists that an SDN-only screen does not cover.

investigator.supplier: Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology Co., Ltd.
reasons: The registry answer is for "SHENZHEN LDROBOT CO.,LTD", registration 91440300MA5ETL7D53 (not active), not "Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology Co., Ltd.": it does not confirm the supplier, so a person confirms the company before paying it.
"Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology Co., Ltd.": no match, but only one list was searched (OFAC SDN), so other sanctions and export-control lists are unchecked.
A search answer ties the supplier to a risk term, so a person should read it: "USA considers sanctions against Hikvision: USA considers sanctions against Hikvision."

The invoice asks for payment by direct bank transfer outside Alibaba.com's Trade Assurance, so the order loses that protection: confirm the change with the supplier through the marketplace before paying.

The bank account belongs to "Hong Kong Shengtai Trading Limited", not to "Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology Co., Ltd.": an invoice that pays someone other than the supplier is held until the supplier confirms the account through a channel already on file.
